items.item: The header shows the delivery note number, issue date, source sales order or transfer number and dispatching warehouse, each with a visible label, and every date on the note uses one unambiguous format (such as 06 Nov 2026)
items.evidence: Note No., Date ("November 7, 2026") and Order Ref. (SO-88291) are labelled in the title band/#metaGrid, but dispatching warehouse has no labelled field — it's only inline prose in #senderBlock: "Warehouse: WH-04 — Charlotte DC · VAT/EIN: 58-3301942". Date formats also disagree across the note: header uses shipment.date = "November 7, 2026" while the footer uses `new Date().toLocaleString("en-US",{dateStyle:"medium",timeStyle:"short"})` which renders as "Nov 9, 2026, 8:48 AM" — two different date formats on one document.

items.item: Sender (company name, address, tax ID), recipient (customer name, delivery address, contact person and phone) and carrier (carrier name, vehicle plate or driver name) appear in three separately labelled blocks
items.evidence: Sender is a labelled block ("Shipped From" / #senderBlock with name, address, tax ID) and recipient info is split across "Customer" (#customerBlock) and "Deliver To" (#deliverBlock) blocks, but carrier fields (Carrier, Vehicle Reg., Driver) are just <dt>/<dd> rows inside the generic #metaGrid dl mixed with Date/PO Number/Incoterm/Page — there is no separately labelled "Carrier" block.

items.item: The goods are in a real <table> with column headers in <thead>, giving per line: line number, item code, description, unit of measure, quantity ordered, quantity delivered and lot or serial number, with quantities right-aligned
items.evidence: A real <table> with <thead>/<th scope="col"> headers (#, Item Code, Description, Ordered, Shipped, UoM, Packages, Notes) is present and Ordered/Shipped columns are right-aligned (class="text-right"), but no lot or serial number column exists at all — the `items` data objects only have `{code, desc, ordered, shipped, uom, packages, note}`.

items.item: A line delivered short of the ordered quantity states the outstanding amount in words (such as "Backorder: 4 pcs") rather than by colour alone
items.evidence: Row 3 (SKU-30891, ordered 25 / shipped 24) is flagged with `bg-amber-50` and the note text "Short-shipped — backorder BO-1187", but this never states the outstanding quantity (1 unit) in words — it references a backorder ticket number, not an amount like "Backorder: 1 pcs".

items.item: A footer gives the total quantity delivered, the number of packages and the gross weight with its unit, and the quantity total equals the sum of the lines
items.evidence: <tfoot> shows #totalShipped (159, correctly summed from the 6 lines: 12+40+24+60+8+15) and #totalPackages ("9 pkgs"), but no gross weight field exists anywhere in the markup or script.

items.item: Signature boxes are provided for the warehouse keeper (issued by), the driver or carrier and the receiver, each with room for printed name, signature and date, plus a remarks area for the condition of the goods on receipt
items.evidence: Three labelled columns "Dispatched By (Warehouse)", "Carrier / Driver", "Received By (Customer)" each contain Signature / "Printed name & …" / Date lines (.sig-line divs), and a "Condition on Receipt" section provides Good condition/Damaged/Partial checkboxes plus a blank remarks line for damage/partial notes.

items.item: A Print control that is a real <button> starts printing, and an @media print stylesheet hides the app navigation and on-screen controls, sets page margins and keeps the signature block from splitting across pages
items.evidence: `<button id="printBtn">` calls `window.print()` and `@media print` hides `.no-print` and sets `@page { size: A4; margin: 12mm; }`, but the print CSS only applies `page-break-inside: avoid` to `tr` (table rows) — no rule protects the signature grid div from splitting across a page break.

items.item: The note's status (such as Draft, Dispatched, Delivered or Cancelled) is shown in words next to its number, and a draft or cancelled note prints with a visible "DRAFT" or "CANCELLED" mark so it cannot pass as a valid dispatch document
items.evidence: A "Dispatched" badge (`Dispatched`) sits next to the note number, but the status is a hardcoded string with no conditional logic in the script — there is no mechanism anywhere that would render a DRAFT/CANCELLED watermark if the status were different.

items.item: A loading state is present, and a note that fails to load or does not exist shows a message with Retry and a link back to the delivery note list, never an empty template with blank fields
items.evidence: No loading indicator, error state, Retry control or back-link exists; all content (`sender`, `customer`, `deliverTo`, `shipment`, `items`) is hardcoded JS data rendered synchronously, as acknowledged by the on-screen caption "Mock data shown for layout preview only — use the Print button above for a clean printout."

notes: Document is a static mock (hardcoded JS objects, no fetch/loading/error handling). Audit flags (text-contrast, tabular-nums, numeric-align on the # column, uppercase-text, missing tel:/mailto: links, shadow-over-border) are consistent with the manual findings above. 'tracked-uppercase-labels' is pervasive: 'SHIPPED FROM', 'DELIVERY NOTE', 'NOTE NO.', 'CUSTOMER', 'DELIVER TO', 'GOODS SHIPPED', all metaGrid <dt> labels, and all signature captions use uppercase + tracking-wide/tracking-[0.2em].
